subject: Axion demo: curated model slate + prioritization
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@axion.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-07T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Axion demo: curated model slate + prioritization

Hi Charlie — great session today, thanks for walking us through the merchant fraud flows and the real-time scoring constraints. Quick written recap and our recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary workload: short chat-like prompts + structured merchant attributes leading to a binary fraud decision and an explanation snippet for agent UX.
- SLOs: 99th percentile latency target 220ms (in-region), burst to 400ms tolerable.
- Cost: target ~ $0.60–0.90 per 1k inference requests at expected qps after initial rollout.
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction required; audit logs must be retained for 90 days.

Our recommended shortlists (high level):
1) Candidate A (8-bit quantized Mistral-7B variant): best cost/latency balance. Median latency ~95ms, 99p ~180ms on a single T4-equivalent instance. Strong at intent/slot extraction with our prompt templates (see attached).
2) Candidate B (13B distilled open model): higher quality on edge cases and rare merchant patterns; median 170ms, 99p 320ms. Cost premium ~2.4x vs Candidate A.
3) Candidate C (larger ensemble fallback / 34B LLM): reserved for escalations and complex disputes where explanation depth matters. Not for primary inference due to cost and latency, but valuable for A/B with low percentage traffic.

Immediate next steps we propose:
- Technical POC: run 48h throughput & latency run on a representative production trace (we'll provide the harness).
- Prompt set delivery: we attached an initial prompt pack (axion_prompt_pack_v1.zip) containing the canonical prompts used in our bench runs. Please review and flag any domain terms you want us to add.
- Regression metrics: establish baseline metrics (accuracy on intent classification, hallucination rate on rationale snippets, mean token length). We'll instrument these in the POC.

Attachments referenced in thread:
- axion_prompt_pack_v1.zip (prompt templates + expected response examples)
- inference_benchmarks_axion_202709.csv (raw run results)

Charlie — does the plan align with your procurement timeline? If so we can schedule the POC and the procurement kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 99p latency target of 220ms is for the in-region (US east) path; we have occasional cross-region fallbacks that can spike. Can you confirm expected 99p in region vs cross-region for Candidate A?
- For costing, our CFO asked for a simple breakout: per-request cost at 10k qps sustained vs 2k qps pilot. Can you include that in the POC deliverable?
- On data handling: we need explicit confirmation that PII redaction happens prior to any logging for hosted inference. If not, point us to Private deployment options.

Procurement: we can run the POC as soon as we have a straightforward SOW and a 30-day test license. Our preferred start is 2027-09-20.

Team — forwarding Charlie's notes. Procurement wants a date (pref 20th) and we need a tight POC scope that answers: latency at 99p in-region vs cross-region, per-request cost at two throughput levels, and PII handling controls (hosted vs Private).

Proposed POC scope (short):
- 48h run on representative trace (we have permission to use anonymized trace from Charlie).
- Test candidates: Candidate A (quantized 7B), Candidate B (13B distill), small % traffic to Candidate C (34B) for N=1000 escalation queries.
- Measurements: median/99p latency (in-region and cross-region), tokens-per-request, costs, accuracy on a 500-sample labelled holdout, hallucination rate (binary label), and tokenized output length distribution.
- Deliverables: summary deck, raw CSVs, prompt pack, and a short ops-runbook for rollout.

I'm assigning the bench runs to Marissa + Karthik to scope infra and estimate cost. Ben, please review contract/30-day test license language and prepare a one-page SOW.

Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Charlie Nguyen <charlie@axion.ai>
Date: 2027-09-20T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Axion demo: curated model slate + prioritization — POC plan + prioritized slate

Hi all — had the bench team run an initial dry pass on the sanitized sample trace Charlie shared. Below are prioritized recommendations plus the rationale and a compact ops plan.

Summary prioritized slate (recommended rollout):
- Phase 0 (pilot, 2k qps): Candidate A (quant-7B) as primary. Rationale: lowest unit cost, stable latency, solid accuracy on canonical intents (accuracy 93.8% on holdout). 99p observed ~190ms in-region; cross-region 99p ~330ms (due to network tail).
- Phase 1 (scale to 10k qps): Candidate A with KV prefix caching + dynamic batching; switch to dedicated instances for predictable 99p. Expected cost delta vs pilot: ~+25% for reserved capacity overhead but per-request compute cost drops ~18% because of batching.
- Phase 2 (safety/fallback): Candidate B as canary for 5% traffic and Candidate C (34B) for manual escalation/A/B on cases where explanation depth matters. Candidate B measured accuracy 96.1% on edge-case set; median latency 170ms but 99p 320ms.

Quantitative highlights (dry pass):
- Candidate A: median latency 92ms, 99p 190ms; tokens/request 42; cost estimate (hosted) ~$0.18 per 1k tokens equivalent (pilot); estimated monthly cost at 10k qps sustained ~ $9k/day compute (region price assumption).
- Candidate B: median 170ms, 99p 320ms; better recall on rare merchant categories (F1 uplift +2.3 points vs A). Cost ~2.3x Candidate A.
- Candidate C: high-quality explanations, heavy cost; only for <0.1% of traffic as a last-resort.

Regression concerns & guardrails:
- Prompt drift: recommend maintaining a locked 'regression prompt pack' (attached) used for continuous eval runs; any edits must be versioned and gated by a >2% quality delta alert.
- Metric plateau: track hallucination rate weekly; set an alert at >1.5x baseline.
- Token inflation: monitor median token length by route — increases indicate prompt creep or untrimmed inputs.

Attachments (for POC):
- inference_benchmarks_axion_202709.csv (raw run CSV)
- axion_prompt_pack_v1.zip (canonical & regression prompts)
- axion_latency_cost_estimates.pdf (summary slides with cost math)

Ops & timeline:
- 2027-09-20: start POC (48h bench + 24h regression runs)
- 2027-09-24: deliver POC deck + recommendation to Charlie + SOW draft
- After POC: plan for 2-week pilot, then dedicated capacity if all SLOs met.

Charlie — confirming we can start today as requested. Ben, can you push the 30-day license SOW by EOD? Karthik, Marissa will sync on infra sizing (I assigned follow-up Jira ticket INF-AX-88).

Thanks,
Marissa
